answers.answer: Shuffle the nine region cards, reveal the top one, and place the King there. Each player takes another region card for their home region and puts their Grande there. Each takes ten Caballeros: two in the home region beside the Grande, one on the first success-track space, and seven in their court.
answers.evidence: “Shuffle the nine region cards; reveal the top card and put the King in that region… another region card to determine their home region… ten Caballeros: two… home region… one… success track… seven… court.”

answers.answer: In round 1, the players choose who starts playing power cards. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round starts; others play clockwise. No power-card value already played that round may be matched.
answers.evidence: “Players choose who begins… later, the player who took the last turn… begins. Others play clockwise. No value already played this round may be matched.”

answers.answer: Players take turns in descending power-card value. At the start of their turn, each recruits up to the allowance pictured on their power card from provinces to court; they may recruit fewer. This happens before choosing an action card.
answers.evidence: “At the start of your turn recruit up to… from the provinces into your court… After recruitment, choose an available face-up action card.”

answers.answer: If your provinces lack enough of your Caballeros, you may take your own pieces from the board to make up the difference. The King's region cannot supply them, and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.
answers.evidence: “If there are insufficient Caballeros of your color in the provinces, you may take your own from the board… The King's region remains taboo and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.”

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment is from your court to regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo. You may divide the card's allowance among those destinations, but the printed number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none.
answers.evidence: “Move them from your court to any regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo, dividing the allowance freely… number is a maximum.”

answers.answer: Yes. Complete ordinary deployment and the special action in either order, but complete one activity before starting the other; neither can be split or interleaved. You may decline the special action.
answers.evidence: “Do them in either order… neither may be split or interleaved… You may decline the special action.”

answers.answer: After a turn, set aside its selected action card so later players cannot choose it. After all players have taken turns, discard remaining face-up action cards. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: “Lay aside the selected action card… After every player… discard any remaining… The King card is revealed again every round and never permanently discarded.”

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King's region. It may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected; actions that move the King are the exception to the movement restriction.
answers.evidence: “no Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of it… It may still be scored. Actions that move the King… changes which region is protected.”

answers.answer: Announce clearly how many Caballeros you put in the Castillo. They may enter regardless of the King's location. No action removes them; they leave only during general scoring.
answers.evidence: “Whenever adding Caballeros… any or all may go into the Castillo, regardless of the King's location. Announce clearly how many… No action removes… leave only during general scoring.”

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. First, all players secretly set disks to a board region other than the King's region and place them face down, before uncovering the Castillo. Second, score the Castillo. Third, reveal disks and move each player's Castillo pieces to that one chosen region (with illegal King-region selections redirected to court). Replace the empty Castillo. Fourth, score the nine regions in scoring-track order.
answers.evidence: “After rounds 3, 6 and 9”; ordered stages: “Secretly select destinations before uncovering the Castillo”; “Score the Castillo”; “Reveal disks and empty the Castillo”; “Score the nine regions.”

answers.answer: A player must send all their Castillo Caballeros to one region, not split them, and may not choose the King's region or keep them in the Castillo. If the King's region was illegally selected, those pieces go to that player's court.
answers.evidence: “All that player's Castillo Caballeros must go to one region. Choosing the King's region is prohibited… none may be retained inside or split… If someone illegally selected the King's region, their pieces go to their court.”

answers.answer: The three tied players score 3 points each, and the player with three Caballeros scores 1 point. Grandes do not count toward majority; only Caballeros count.
answers.evidence: Example: “On 5/3/1, counts 4,4,4,3 score 3,3,3,1.” “Only Caballeros count… A Grande… contributes zero Caballeros.”

answers.answer: The players with counts 4, 3, 2, and 2 score 6, 4, 0, and 0 respectively.

In a two-player game only first place can pay; in a three-player game first and second can pay. In a two-player tie for first, neither scores because the tie shifts them to second, which is outside the payable rank cutoff.
answers.evidence: “Two players: only first place can pay. Three players: only first and second… apply the player-count cutoff after this rank shift: a two-player tie for first pays neither.”

answers.answer: The King's bonus is +2 for the sole majority holder in the King's region; the home bonus is +2 if the sole majority holder has their own Grande there. Apply them whenever the region is scored, including special scoring. Neither is awarded on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: “Bonuses apply whenever the relevant region is scored, including special scorings”; “King's bonus: +2… sole”; “Home bonus: +2… own Grande”; “Neither bonus… on a tie.”

answers.answer: Specially scoring the Castillo does not empty it or redistribute its Caballeros. Reveal and score its contents, then cover the same pieces again; redistribution waits until general scoring.
answers.evidence: “Special scoring of the Castillo reveals and scores its contents, then covers them again without redistribution.”

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be introduced at or moved to the Castillo. It may not move into or out of the King's region. The two scoreboards cannot be stacked, and they must remain right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0, without rotation to invent values.
answers.evidence: “Castillo is allowed. No movement into or out of the King's region. The two mobile scoreboards cannot be stacked… right side up… never reversed or rotated.”

answers.answer: Move your Grande to another region, but not into the King's region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King's region. Other Grandes may already be at the destination. The destination becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: “Move your Grande to another region except the King's region or Castillo. It cannot leave the King's region. A destination may already contain several Grandes. The destination becomes your new home region.”

answers.answer: The recovery action returns any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the card used that turn. You need not reveal which card you chose, though taking the visible top card will be apparent.
answers.evidence: “Return any one of your played power cards to hand, including the one played this turn. You need not reveal which.”

answers.answer: The game ends after completing all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins; no additional endgame tiebreaker is given.
answers.evidence: “Finish all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. Whoever is furthest along the success track wins. The source gives no additional endgame tiebreaker.”

answers.answer: Separate action cards into stacks by the 1–5 Caballeros printed on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place them face down beside the board. At the start of each round, reveal the top card of each of the five stacks (five cards). The standard round marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: “Separate action cards into stacks by the 1–5 Caballeros… Shuffle each stack separately”; reveal “the top card of each of the five action stacks”; “Start the round marker at 1.”

answers.answer: Played power cards are not returned to hand; they remain in each player's face-up used stack, with only the top card visible. A special action can recover a played card.
answers.evidence: “Played cards remain in each player's face-up used stack with only the top card visible… A special action can recover a played card.”

answers.answer: If the King is moved before ordinary deployment, the King's new position determines adjacent deployment destinations. The King card lets you put the King in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: “If you move the King before ordinary deployment, use his new position”; King card: “put the King in any region except Castillo.”

answers.answer: Keep the Veto card in front of you. It can stop one special action during this round or the next, but cannot stop the ordinary deployment part of an action card.
answers.evidence: “Put the card before you and retain it to stop one special action during this round or the next. It cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion.”

answers.answer: While Veto is held, other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as the player starts: you can stop an announced action before execution or prevent the remaining part of an incomplete special action. A completed action cannot be vetoed. You may prevent just part; executed parts are not undone.
answers.evidence: “Other players must announce special actions before executing them… Object as soon as the player starts… Completed actions cannot be vetoed… already executed parts are not undone.”

answers.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: “Discard after using the veto once; if unused, discard at the end of the next round.”

answers.answer: All fellow players send all Caballeros in their courts to the provinces; the selecting player is unaffected. A player with an empty court sends none.
answers.evidence: “Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces; an empty court sends none. The selecting player is unaffected.”

answers.answer: The fellow player with two in court sends both (all they have if fewer than three); you, the selecting player, are unaffected and keep your five.
answers.evidence: “Every fellow player sends three court Caballeros to the provinces, or all they have if fewer than three. The selecting player is unaffected.”

answers.answer: The detailed execution paragraph and printed card require each player, including the selecting player, to send three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Start with the player to the selector's left and proceed clockwise, with the selector last. Each chooses their own pieces from any regions and/or their court, never from the King's region or Castillo. No shortfall rule is supplied if someone has fewer than three eligible pieces. The bold heading instead says “fellow players.”
answers.evidence: “The detailed execution paragraph and printed card say each player, including the selecting player… three own Caballeros… Start with… left… selecting player last… any regions and/or their court, never the King's region or Castillo”; “source supplies no explicit shortfall rule.” Heading discrepancy: “fellow players”.

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each selected piece to its owner's provinces. Pieces cannot be taken from courts, the King's region, or the Castillo. The source gives no fallback if a player has no eligible piece.
answers.evidence: “The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves… No taking from courts, the King's region or Castillo”; “no explicit fallback when a player has no eligible piece.”

answers.answer: Affected fellow players choose secretly and simultaneously on their disks, then reveal together. Each must choose a region containing at least two of that player's Caballeros, and return two to the provinces.
answers.evidence: “Each affected fellow player secretly chooses one region on their disk, with choices simultaneous and revealed together. It must contain at least two of that player's Caballeros; return two.”

answers.answer: If the player has at most one in every region, they choose a region with one Caballero and return that one to the provinces. (The summary does not verify a fallback for the different case where two or more are only in the protected King's region and other regions have singletons.)
answers.evidence: “The stated singleton fallback applies if the player has at most one in every region: choose a region with one and return that one.”

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses a region with at least one of their Caballeros on a disk; choices are revealed simultaneously. They return all their own Caballeros in that region to the provinces. A player with none in any region is unaffected.
answers.evidence: “Simultaneous secret disk selection, then reveal together. Each affected fellow player chooses a region with at least one… returns all their own there… A player with none in any region is unaffected.”

answers.answer: Yes, choose any region including the King's region or Castillo. Use normal region-scoring rules, applicable rank limits and bonuses. If Castillo is chosen, score it and cover the same pieces again; do not redistribute them.
answers.evidence: “Choose any region, including the King's region or Castillo. Use normal region-scoring rules, applicable rank limits and bonuses. If Castillo is chosen, score it and cover the same pieces again; do not distribute them.”

answers.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia (4/2/0), Catalonia (4/2/1), and Seville (4/3/1). Eligibility is based on the current first value: Galicia with a mobile 8/4/0 is excluded, while Granada with 4/0/0 is included. Applicable bonuses apply to these special scorings.
answers.evidence: “All 4-value regions… current first value is 4. Printed group: Galicia 4/2/0, Catalonia 4/2/1, Seville 4/3/1… A mobile 8/4/0 in Galicia removes it… 4/0/0 in Granada adds Granada”; special scorings: “Applicable home and King's bonuses apply.”

answers.answer: The printed 5-value group is Basque Country (5/3/1), Aragon (5/4/1), and Valencia (5/3/2). The printed 6-and-7 group is Old Castile (6/4/2), New Castile (7/4/2), and Granada (6/3/1). Current first value determines the group when mobile scoreboards are present. Castillo is not scored by all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: “All 5-value regions: Current first value 5. Printed group…”; “All 6- and 7-value regions: Current first value 6 or 7…”. “Castillo is not scored.”

answers.answer: Only sole first places score; lower ranks receive nothing. A tie for first scores nothing because it would normally pay second place. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: “Only sole first places score; other ranks get nothing. A tie for first scores nothing… Excludes Castillo.”

answers.answer: Score all board regions tied for the most Caballeros. The Castillo is neither considered nor scored, even if it contains more than either region.
answers.evidence: “Compare total Caballeros in each board region. Score all regions tied for the most. Castillo is neither considered nor scored.”

answers.answer: Compare nonempty board regions and score all regions tied for the least. Empty regions and the Castillo are neither considered nor scored.
answers.evidence: “Compare nonempty board regions; score all tied for the least. Empty regions and Castillo are neither considered nor scored.”

answers.answer: All fellow players move all their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each affected player secretly picks another region on their disk; choices are revealed simultaneously and their pieces move to those destinations. A player choosing the King's region or the region being vacated sends their pieces to their court instead. (The King's-region taboo prevents taking pieces out of that region.)
answers.evidence: “all fellow players move all their own Caballeros out… secretly chooses another region… reveal choices simultaneously… Choosing the King's region or the region being vacated sends… to their court… taboo prevents taking pieces out of the King's region.”

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King to a neighboring region, at most one region away. The King card can put him in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: “Royal Adviser: Move the King into a neighboring region, no more than one region away”; King card: “any region except Castillo.”

answers.answer: The Court moves two of your own Caballeros from provinces to your court. It is separate from a 4-stack card's ordinary deployment of up to four from court to board; either complete activity may go first.
answers.evidence: “Move two of your own Caballeros from provinces to court… separate from the card's ordinary up-to-four court-to-board deployment; either complete activity can go first.”

answers.answer: All players secretly choose regions on disks and reveal simultaneously. The disk allows the nine board regions, including the King's region, but not Castillo. Score each uniquely chosen region under normal rules; a region chosen by multiple players is not scored.
answers.evidence: “All players choose secretly on disks and reveal simultaneously… nine board regions, including the King's region, but not Castillo… Score each uniquely chosen region… If multiple players chose a region, it is not scored.”

answers.answer: You may take all your own Caballeros from one region and distribute them among other regions and/or the Castillo; you may return some to the original region. Origins exclude the King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King's region but may include Castillo. (Ordinary deployment is separate and remains adjacent to the King.)
answers.evidence: “Take all your own from one region and distribute among other regions and/or Castillo. You may return some to the original region”; table note: “origins… exclude the King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King's region but may include the Castillo.”

answers.answer: The special action adds up to two more of your own Caballeros from court; combined with the normal deployment, up to three may enter the board. Only the normal deployment requires adjacency; the two extra pieces may go to any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: “Up to two additional own Caballeros from court to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. With the normal one, up to three enter the board, but only the normal one requires adjacency.”

answers.answer: You choose only one of the two special alternatives, not both. The normal up-to-one deployment still applies.
answers.evidence: “Choose one of the preceding special actions, not both. Normal deployment still applies.”

answers.answer: Up to five pieces may come from one origin region. They may be your own and/or foreign pieces, but not from multiple origin regions. Distribute them to other non-King regions and/or the Castillo.
answers.evidence: “Up to five own and/or foreign Caballeros from one origin region, distributed to other non-King regions and/or Castillo.”

answers.answer: You may move up to three foreign (other players') Caballeros, using any non-King board regions, including multiple origins; your own pieces cannot be included. Castillo is never a source. Destinations may be any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: “Up to three other players' Caballeros from any non-King board regions, including multiple origins, never from Castillo. Destinations: any non-King regions and/or Castillo.”

answers.answer: The any-three action moves up to three own and/or foreign pieces from any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. The any-four action moves up to four own and/or foreign pieces from any non-King origins to other non-King regions and/or Castillo. The summary specifies the any-four destination wording as “other regions.”
answers.evidence: “Any three… own and/or foreign… any non-King origin regions to any non-King regions and/or Castillo”; “Any four… any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo.”

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros; these are separate ownership allowances. They may come from any regions, with multiple origins permitted. The entry says “from any regions” and the general table note applies: origins exclude the King's region and Castillo. Destinations are any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: “Up to two of your own plus two foreign, from any regions; these are separate ownership allowances.” General table note: “All table entries remain subject to the taboo and Castillo rules above.” Sources exclude King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude King's region and may include Castillo.

answers.answer: Move up to four Caballeros, own only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: “Up to four own only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo.”

answers.answer: On the 4-stack secret-choice scoring action, the King's region may be selected but Castillo may not. By contrast, the action that lets its player pick one location to score allows either the King's region or Castillo.
answers.evidence: 4-stack: “disk permits the nine board regions, including the King's region, but not Castillo”; Stack 2: “Choose any region, including the King's region or Castillo.”

answers.answer: The mobile scoreboards begin beside the board. On the action, you may introduce one from beside the board or move one already on the board to a different region.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Place both mobile scoreboards beside the board”; action: “Introduce a scoreboard from beside the board or move one already on it to a different region.”
